title: View, save, or delete email attachments in Mail on Mac
observation: Apple says Remove Attachments keeps the message but removes its attachments, and for IMAP accounts it also deletes those attachments from the mail server.
product_implication: Treat Mail's owner action as a remote mutation for IMAP, not a local cache purge. Show the account type and server effect before approval.
quality_note: First-party Apple documentation. It defines current product behavior but says nothing about how often users invoke it.

title: Delete emails and manage storage in Mail on Mac
observation: Apple separates server storage, Mac-only mailboxes, saved attachments, IMAP Trash, and POP server copies. Emptying Trash can remove server messages.
product_implication: Model each mailbox by account protocol and location. A visible Mail folder can be local-only, server-backed, or a pending deletion queue.
quality_note: First-party Apple documentation. It is an owner fact, not user-behavior evidence.

title: Change Mailbox Behaviours settings in Mail on Mac
observation: Mail can map Drafts, Sent, Junk, Trash, and Archive to server mailboxes or Mac-only mailboxes, and provider retention can override local settings.
product_implication: Do not classify mailbox files by folder name alone. Read account mappings and explain whether deletion changes local state, server state, or both.
quality_note: First-party Apple documentation. Settings and labels can vary by macOS version.

title: Change Account Information settings in Mail on Mac
observation: Mail always downloads media attachments and can download all, recent, or no other attachment types into a special Library folder.
product_implication: Show the configured attachment-download policy. Offer the owner control before any raw-folder action.
quality_note: First-party Apple documentation. It describes configuration, not actual current completeness of a local store.

title: Mail cache reported at 358 GB
observation: A Mac user reported 358 GB attributed to work mail and did not want to delete messages because they were business records.
product_implication: Treat large Mail storage as a preservation case first. Separate records, attachments, indexes, and opened-download copies before offering action.
quality_note: Direct first-person report on Apple's support community. It proves one need and one storage symptom, not prevalence or the exact accounting cause.

title: Deleting Mail downloads did not reduce the reported Mail size
observation: A user deleted old files from a Mail download location, but macOS still reported about 14 GB for Mail.
product_implication: Do not promise reclaim from a path size or category label alone. Rescan allocated bytes after the owner action and explain delayed storage accounting.
quality_note: Direct first-person report on Apple's support community. The report does not prove which remaining Mail component held the space.

title: Drafts mailbox grew beyond 100 GB
observation: A user reported a Drafts mailbox above 100 GB and noted that deleting the mailbox file would permanently delete drafts.
product_implication: Draft mailboxes are user work even when they look like runaway storage. Require item-level review or an owner repair path, never a broad safe label.
quality_note: Direct first-person report on Apple's support community. It establishes the reported risk, not the root cause or frequency.

title: Manual Mail cache reset suggested for stubborn storage
observation: A community thread mixes built-in attachment cleanup with advice to move Mail data and container folders so the app rebuilds them.
product_implication: Community cleanup recipes are not safe policy. Tessera should prefer documented owner controls and mark broad profile resets as high-risk recovery actions.
quality_note: Owner-hosted community content, not Apple documentation. Advice may be wrong or version-specific and is recorded as a counterexample.

title: Keep your messages up to date with iCloud
observation: With Messages in iCloud, only recently accessed messages may stay local, and sends, receives, and deletions propagate across devices.
product_implication: A local attachment can be an evictable cloud copy, but only after Tessera verifies Messages in iCloud, account health, and remote availability.
quality_note: First-party Apple documentation. It defines the sync model, not a guarantee that every item is currently recoverable.

title: Delete messages and conversations in Messages on Mac
observation: Deleted Messages content stays recoverable for up to 30 days, but iCloud deletion propagates across devices and shorter Keep Messages settings remove conversations and attachments automatically.
product_implication: Use the owner deletion surface and show the recovery window, Keep Messages setting, and cross-device effect before confirmation.
quality_note: First-party Apple documentation. Retention details can change by OS version and account state.

title: Change General settings in Messages on Mac
observation: Messages exposes a Keep Messages period, after which conversations are removed automatically.
product_implication: Report configured retention as a cause of growth or loss. Do not describe retained attachments as unexplained cache.
quality_note: First-party Apple documentation. It describes the control, not the user's intent.

title: Messages attachments and caches reached 27 GB
observation: A user reported 27 GB under Messages and said manual removal made cloud-backed attachments available for later download.
product_implication: Treat this as a hypothesis to verify, not a deletion rule. Confirm iCloud backing for each item and use an owner-supported eviction method if one exists.
quality_note: Direct first-person report on Apple's community. The claimed re-download behavior is not owner documentation and may not cover local-only SMS or failed sync.

title: Zeroing the Messages database removed visible history
observation: A user reported that zeroing chat database files removed message history from the app and that restoring the files restored it.
product_implication: Protect chat.db and its WAL and SHM files as one live database group. Never offer them as cache or edit them while Messages is active.
quality_note: Direct first-person report on Apple's community. It proves a destructive boundary, not a supported recovery procedure.

title: About accounts and folders in Notes on Mac
observation: Notes can store content in iCloud or On My Mac. Moving between accounts can lose formatting or attachment editability, and some accounts have no Recently Deleted recovery.
product_implication: Classify each note store by account. Protect On My Mac data and explain format loss before any owner move or account reset.
quality_note: First-party Apple documentation. It defines account boundaries and documented loss cases.

title: Search your notes on Mac
observation: Notes search spans accounts and Recently Deleted, but locked notes expose only titles to search; the attachment browser is a separate content view.
product_implication: Do not infer missing content from an index result. Keep search indexes separate from note bodies, locked content, and attachment stores.
quality_note: First-party Apple documentation. It describes visible search behavior, not internal file safety.

title: Unsynced month of Notes remained only on the Mac
observation: A user with thousands of notes reported a month of edits absent from iCloud while a 470 MB local Notes database still existed on the Mac.
product_implication: A stale sync state makes the local database authoritative for recent work. Block cleanup and prompt for export or backup before account changes.
quality_note: Direct first-person report on Apple's support community. It proves one sync-gap scenario, not prevalence.

title: On My Mac notes appeared missing after an upgrade
observation: A user reported that locally stored notes disappeared after a macOS upgrade and reappeared after changing the iCloud Notes setting.
product_implication: An inactive or hidden local account is not an abandoned store. Compare database contents and account visibility before suggesting cleanup.
quality_note: Direct first-person report on Apple's support community. It records a visibility failure, not physical deletion.

title: Notes attachments stalled until a verified cloud redownload
observation: A user reported hundreds of Notes attachments unavailable after migration; toggling sync helped only after the attachments were confirmed on iCloud.com.
product_implication: Require remote proof before treating local note attachments as replaceable. A sync toggle is unsafe when the remote copy is incomplete.
quality_note: Direct first-person report on Apple's support community. It shows a condition for safe redownload, not a universal repair.

title: Save, download or remove episodes in Podcasts on Mac
observation: Podcasts separates saved episodes from downloaded copies. Unsave does not necessarily remove a download, while Remove Download frees local storage.
product_implication: Present the owner Remove Download action and preserve library state. Do not delete podcast files by path.
quality_note: First-party Apple documentation. It defines the supported local-eviction action.

title: Change settings in Podcasts on Mac
observation: Podcasts can sync library state, download saved episodes, limit automatic downloads, and remove played downloads after 24 hours.
product_implication: Explain which setting caused growth and offer a future retention change separately from removing current downloads.
quality_note: First-party Apple documentation. Settings describe policy, not the actual current file set.

title: User sought one action to remove many podcast downloads
observation: A user cleaning disk space found per-show and Storage settings paths for removing many downloaded episodes.
product_implication: Offer a deep link or guided owner action with a before and after size check when the app lacks an obvious bulk control.
quality_note: Direct first-person support exchange. It shows discoverability friction, not frequency.

title: Deleted podcast downloads kept returning
observation: A user reported removed episodes returning until automatic downloads were disabled and an update completed.
product_implication: A cleanup is incomplete if the creation rule remains active. Pair removal with the exact automatic-download cause and verify recurrence later.
quality_note: Direct first-person report on Apple's support community. It proves one recurrence path, not all causes of redownload.

title: Podcast documents and data persisted after uninstall
observation: A user reported 29 GB of Podcasts documents and data remaining after app deletion and reinstall, with no visible downloaded episodes.
product_implication: Distinguish offloaded app data, active downloads, and stale accounting. Do not equate app removal with data removal or promise immediate reclaim.
quality_note: Direct first-person report on Apple's support community. The exact retained component was not established.

title: Clear the cache in Outlook for Mac
observation: Microsoft warns that Empty Cache deletes information not synchronized with Exchange, including a contact's mail certificate, before redownloading server items.
product_implication: Require server comparison and a local export before Outlook cache reset. Label the action as destructive to unsynced state.
quality_note: First-party Microsoft documentation. It is strong owner evidence for the reset boundary.

title: Remove or delete attachments in Outlook
observation: Outlook's attachment action depends on client type; desktop can remove received attachments while web clients may require deleting the email.
product_implication: Choose the owner action by Outlook mode and account. Show whether the message, attachment, or server mailbox changes.
quality_note: First-party Microsoft documentation. Version-specific behavior requires adapter checks.

title: About On My Computer folders in Outlook for Mac
observation: Outlook for Mac can keep items in On My Computer folders that exist only on that Mac and do not synchronize with a mail server.
product_implication: Protect On My Computer stores as local-only records. Never include them in a server-cache reset or infer a remote backup.
quality_note: First-party Microsoft documentation. It defines the local-only boundary.

title: Outlook for Mac stopped loading email bodies
observation: A Mac user reported missing message bodies across accounts; the accepted guidance warned that Reset Account can delete unsynced drafts.
product_implication: Before reset, compare web and desktop state and enumerate drafts or local folders absent from the server.
quality_note: Direct user report on Microsoft's Q&A site. Replies include community and moderator guidance; only the reported symptom is behavior evidence.

title: Local Outlook folders stopped opening after cache clearing
observation: A Mac user reported local Outlook folders no longer opening after password and cache changes.
product_implication: Do not include local folders in a generic account repair. Back up the Outlook profile and preserve folder identity before reset.
quality_note: Direct first-person report on Microsoft's Q&A site. The final root cause was not proven.

title: Recent local Outlook calendar data was missing
observation: A Mac user reported recent calendar data missing after profile and import attempts; the account used IMAP, which did not provide a server calendar copy.
product_implication: Treat local Outlook calendar and contact data as profile content when the protocol does not sync it. Block cache cleanup until exported.
quality_note: Direct first-person report on Microsoft's Q&A site. The reply's protocol explanation is context, not prevalence evidence.

title: On My Computer folders disappeared after switching Outlook modes
observation: A Mac user reported important On My Computer folders disappearing after switching to the new Outlook and back, while files still seemed present on disk.
product_implication: A hidden local store is not stale. Detect local database content and app mode before suggesting profile cleanup.
quality_note: Direct first-person report on Microsoft's Q&A site. It records visible loss, not confirmed file deletion.

title: Mac held mail and calendar data missing from Outlook on the web
observation: A user said the Mac still showed missing online mail and calendar history and feared that signing in again would erase the surviving copy.
product_implication: When local data is newer than server state, hard-hold all reset and cleanup actions and offer export first.
quality_note: Direct first-person report on Microsoft's Q&A site. It proves a reported divergence, not its cause.

title: User asked whether Outlook cache clearing would delete local mail
observation: A user paused before resetting an IMAP account because mail was stored on the computer; the answer distinguished server cache from On My Computer folders.
product_implication: The review must name protected local stores and excluded paths, not only what will be removed.
quality_note: Direct question on Microsoft's Q&A site. It shows decision friction and a useful counterexample, not an observed deletion.

title: Outlook local folders appeared empty after an update
observation: A Mac user reported restored On My Computer folders with no visible messages after an Outlook update.
product_implication: Separate index or view repair from data deletion. Preserve the database until an owner export proves the messages are recoverable.
quality_note: Direct first-person report on Microsoft's Q&A site. The report does not establish whether files were deleted.

title: Profiles: where Thunderbird stores messages and user data
observation: Thunderbird stores messages, passwords, settings, and changes in the profile and warns that a local or cloud-synced profile is not itself a backup.
product_implication: Protect the profile as a compound data set. Do not split unknown files from credentials, messages, and account configuration.
quality_note: First-party Thunderbird documentation. It defines owner boundaries and backup requirements.

title: Export your Thunderbird Profile
observation: Thunderbird's export backs up accounts, messages, address books, and settings, but its ZIP workflow supports profiles only up to 2 GB.
product_implication: Before cleanup, offer the owner export when it fits and a closed-app folder copy for larger profiles. Verify the resulting backup.
quality_note: First-party Thunderbird documentation. The 2 GB limit is version-specific owner guidance.

title: Advanced settings in Thunderbird
observation: Thunderbird separates a clearable message cache from folders configured for full offline copies, and compaction removes messages already marked deleted.
product_implication: Only the explicit cache control is a cache action. Offline stores and compaction require account and deletion-state proof.
quality_note: First-party Thunderbird documentation. Older interface labels may differ.

title: Rebuilding the Global Database
observation: Thunderbird documents global-messages-db.sqlite as a rebuildable search index and says to quit before deletion; search stays partial during reindexing.
product_implication: Classify only the exact Gloda database as rebuildable and show temporary search loss, expected rebuild work, and closed-app proof.
quality_note: First-party Thunderbird documentation. It does not make other SQLite files safe.

title: Compacting folders
observation: Thunderbird says mbox compaction rewrites folders to remove messages already marked deleted; maildir does not need this process.
product_implication: Use the owner compaction action after checking store type, free working space, app state, and backup. Do not delete mbox files.
quality_note: First-party Thunderbird documentation. It defines the supported reclaim path.

title: IMAP Synchronization
observation: Headers can remain local while bodies are downloaded on demand; full-text search and offline reading require synchronized message bodies, and local deletions can propagate to the server.
product_implication: Show body coverage and offline intent. Reducing synchronized mail trades disk space for offline access and search completeness.
quality_note: First-party Thunderbird documentation. It describes protocol behavior, not server retention guarantees.

title: Failed move to Local Folders deleted messages from the IMAP server
observation: A reporter described an out-of-space move failure where source IMAP messages were marked deleted before the local destination write succeeded.
product_implication: Require working-space proof and post-copy verification before any mail move. Never clean during a pending or failed move.
quality_note: Direct report and fix discussion in Mozilla's owner issue tracker. It proves the failure mode, not prevalence.

title: Offline move from Local to IMAP lost the message
observation: A reporter moved a local message to IMAP while offline; it vanished when Thunderbird went online and did not return to the source folder.
product_implication: Treat queued offline moves as active writes. Block cleanup of source, destination, and operation state until the server acknowledges the move.
quality_note: Direct report in Mozilla's owner issue tracker. It documents a specific regression path.

title: Offline IMAP drafts were deleted when reconnecting
observation: Users reported saved offline drafts disappearing on reconnect; comments noted that un-compacted mbox data could still contain recoverable drafts.
product_implication: Draft stores and un-compacted deleted records are recovery material. Do not compact or purge them while a draft-loss case is open.
quality_note: Direct first-person reports in Mozilla's issue tracker. The old bug remains useful as a failure and recovery boundary, not current prevalence.

title: Large Gloda index made deletion and reindexing costly
observation: A user reported a large global-messages-db.sqlite hitting a profile quota and said deleting it caused roughly half a day of unusable reindexing.
product_implication: Even a rebuildable index has a time and power cost. Estimate rebuild scope and avoid repeated cleanup loops.
quality_note: Direct report in Mozilla's issue tracker. The time cost is one user's environment, not a benchmark.

title: Large local-to-IMAP move stopped after deleting local copies
observation: A user reported thousands of messages moved from local storage to IMAP, with the transfer stopping after local copies had disappeared.
product_implication: Do not suggest bulk move as cleanup without item counts, server verification, resumability, and a retained source copy.
quality_note: Direct first-person report in Mozilla's owner issue tracker. It proves one partial-transfer loss mode.

title: Deleting the search database did not restore search
observation: A user deleted global-messages-db.sqlite as advised, but indexing failed until an older Thunderbird version rebuilt it.
product_implication: A documented rebuildable file is not guaranteed to rebuild in the current runtime. Verify the index completes before declaring recovery.
quality_note: Direct report in Mozilla's owner tracker. It is a counterexample to a simple delete-and-rebuild promise.

title: Global index reconstruction stalled repeatedly
observation: A user reported that rebuilding global-messages-db.sqlite repeatedly stalled with most mail unindexed.
product_implication: Keep rebuild status visible and do not offer another cleanup while reindexing is active or incomplete.
quality_note: Direct first-person report in Mozilla's issue tracker. It proves one stalled rebuild, not a general rate.

title: Folder compaction could destroy mail under error conditions
observation: The issue records compaction-related cases where locked or failing mail folder files could become empty or lose messages.
product_implication: Require closed-app state, no external file lock, enough working space, and a backup before owner compaction on large mbox stores.
quality_note: Owner issue tracker discussion of historical edge cases. It establishes safeguards, not current prevalence.

title: Imported local mail vanished from search after restart
observation: A user reported imported local messages becoming invisible to conversation search after restart even after rebuilding the global index.
product_implication: Search visibility is not proof of file absence. Preserve local stores and compare mailbox records before cleanup.
quality_note: Direct report in Mozilla's owner issue tracker. It documents index behavior, not message deletion.

title: How to clear cache in Spark
observation: Spark says it caches roughly a month of mail and attachments for offline use, has no built-in cache clear on macOS, and points users to a clean install.
product_implication: Do not treat the whole Spark data folder as a cache. If owner reset is chosen, show offline loss, settings reset, and required sign-in.
quality_note: First-party Spark documentation. It defines current owner behavior and may change with product versions.

title: Email Storage and Backups
observation: Spark says ordinary mail stays on the mail provider, while recent content is cached for offline reading and some team or scheduled features use Spark servers.
product_implication: Classify ordinary server mail separately from Spark-hosted team state and local offline copies. Do not assume one recovery source covers all three.
quality_note: First-party Spark documentation. It describes architecture, not proof that every account has a complete server copy.

title: How to Clean Install Spark
observation: Spark's clean install removes the local data folder, settings, and login information, then relies on Spark account sync to restore accounts and settings.
product_implication: Verify Spark account sync and credentials before the owner reset. Describe the action as a profile reset, not cache deletion.
quality_note: First-party Spark documentation. It is an owner action with explicit state loss.

title: Shared Drafts
observation: Shared drafts and their private comments can contain attachments and live outside ordinary mailbox drafts; deleting a shared draft is permanent.
product_implication: Protect shared-draft state and distinguish it from local mail cache. A mail-server comparison does not prove this collaboration data is safe.
quality_note: First-party Spark documentation. It defines supported shared-draft behavior.

title: Remove data from Spark
observation: Spark's Remove your data action deletes Spark-held account data and can cancel a Stripe subscription; the data cannot be restored through the app.
product_implication: Keep remote account deletion outside disk cleanup. It needs a separate destructive confirmation and audience-safe explanation.
quality_note: First-party Spark documentation. It defines an account action, not local reclaim size.

title: Sync Spark across multiple devices
observation: Spark sync can restore connected account and preference setup on another device and exposes device logout and data removal controls.
product_implication: Check account-sync readiness and active devices before clean install. Do not delete authentication state without a verified sign-in path.
quality_note: First-party Spark documentation. It describes supported sync scope, not mailbox completeness.

title: How to create and manage a Spark team
observation: Deleting a Spark team removes shared drafts and comments that are not available through ordinary email clients or webmail.
product_implication: Do not present team deletion as mail cleanup. Identify Spark-hosted collaboration content and require separate remote-deletion consent.
quality_note: First-party Spark documentation. It establishes a remote-only data boundary.

title: Compose an email in Spark
observation: Spark asks whether to save, delete, or minimize an unsent draft when the composer closes.
product_implication: Treat open and saved drafts as user work and check for active composers before any profile action.
quality_note: First-party Spark documentation. It defines visible draft behavior.

title: Customize data retention in Slack
observation: Workspace policy can permanently delete messages and files, while files linked from third-party services remain at their source.
product_implication: Show workspace retention and file origin. Local cache removal cannot recover content already deleted by server policy.
quality_note: First-party Slack documentation. Policy availability depends on plan and administrator settings.

title: Add files to Slack
observation: Slack separates downloaded local copies from workspace files; deleting an uploaded Slack file is a remote action, while external-service files remain at their origin.
product_implication: Classify Slack downloads, Slack-hosted uploads, and external links separately and show which copy an action changes.
quality_note: First-party Slack documentation. It defines product actions, not current local cache paths.

title: How to read Slack data exports
observation: Slack JSON exports often contain file links rather than files, and deleted or expired content can be absent or inaccessible.
product_implication: Do not call an export a complete backup without downloading referenced files and checking retention coverage.
quality_note: First-party Slack documentation. Export content varies by plan, policy, and scope.

title: Usage limits for free workspaces
observation: Free workspaces can hide older content and permanently delete customer data older than one year on a rolling basis.
product_implication: A local cache may be the last accessible copy of content outside the current server window. Check plan and remote visibility before eviction.
quality_note: First-party Slack documentation. Limits can change, so Tessera needs dated adapter facts.

title: Export your workspace data
observation: Slack export scope depends on plan and role; basic exports can omit private channels, direct messages, and file bytes.
product_implication: Before local eviction, verify that the user can export the needed conversation type and that referenced files are copied.
quality_note: First-party Slack documentation. It defines allowed export scopes, not a complete backup guarantee.

title: Guide to Slack import and export tools
observation: Exports are constrained by retention and organization boundaries, and Slack Connect content follows each organization's policy.
product_implication: Show that one workspace's export cannot prove recoverability of all shared-channel content.
quality_note: First-party Slack documentation. It defines policy boundaries, not user behavior.

title: Send and read messages in Slack
observation: Slack has a Drafts and Sent view and supports bulk draft deletion and scheduled-message management.
product_implication: Treat local draft and scheduled-message state as user work until server visibility is verified. Do not include it in cache cleanup.
quality_note: First-party Slack documentation. It describes visible controls, not file layout.

title: Sign out of Slack
observation: Slack supports per-workspace sign-out and remote sign-out of other sessions, but Enterprise workspaces can change the available action.
product_implication: Preserve tokens unless the user has a verified reauthentication path. Keep session revocation separate from disk cleanup.
quality_note: First-party Slack documentation. It defines account actions, not local storage reclaim.

title: How long Discord keeps your information
observation: Discord says deleting content removes it from other users after cache clearing, but deleting an account can leave shared content displayed after anonymization.
product_implication: Do not describe local cache removal, message deletion, and account deletion as equivalent. Show the remote effect of each action.
quality_note: First-party Discord retention documentation. Some legal retention exceptions remain.

title: How to Delete your Discord Account
observation: Discord account deletion has a 15-day recovery period, then removes account access while servers and anonymized messages can remain.
product_implication: Keep account deletion outside disk cleanup and warn that it is not a message purge.
quality_note: First-party Discord documentation. It defines the owner action and recovery window.

title: Requesting a Copy of your Data
observation: Discord requires a verified account for in-app data requests and cancels the request if the account is disabled or deleted before delivery.
product_implication: If an export is needed, complete and verify it before any sign-out or account action.
quality_note: First-party Discord documentation. It describes request mechanics, not local cache coverage.

title: How to Use Search on Discord
observation: Discord says server search can reach messages and files back to server creation unless a user or policy removes them.
product_implication: Use server search as one recoverability check before local cache removal, but do not assume deleted or inaccessible-server content remains.
quality_note: First-party Discord documentation. Access and retention still depend on server membership and deletion.

title: Inactive Account Deletion
observation: Discord may schedule accounts inactive for two years for deletion; login cancels a pending inactive-account deletion.
product_implication: Do not sign out or remove the only working token during a rescue without checking account access and recovery methods.
quality_note: First-party Discord documentation. It concerns account continuity, not direct disk reclaim.

title: Request for a desktop Clear Cache control
observation: A user reported that Discord stored viewed media locally and that desktop cache clearing required manual third-party steps.
product_implication: If no owner control exists, Tessera should show exact cache-only subpaths and keep profile, tokens, drafts, and local databases excluded.
quality_note: Direct first-person post on Discord's community. The post's legal claims are not used, and one request does not establish prevalence.

title: Deleted account messages remained visible
observation: A user reported that deleting a Discord account left prior messages visible and no longer under the user's control.
product_implication: Explain that account deletion does not erase all sent content. Local cleanup must not be presented as a privacy purge.
quality_note: Direct first-person feedback on Discord's owner-hosted community. It records the observed product effect, not prevalence.

title: Account deletion did not delete message history
observation: A user reported that messages remained after account deletion while the account identity was anonymized.
product_implication: Keep message deletion, account deletion, and local cache clearing as separate actions with separate proof.
quality_note: Direct first-person feedback on Discord's community. It confirms a reported expectation gap, not how often it occurs.

title: I cannot reconnect to Microsoft Teams
observation: Microsoft says the older Mac cache-reset path removes web cache, thumbnails, local message history, display images, and add-ons.
product_implication: Do not label the whole Teams Application Support folder as disposable cache. Show the state categories the owner reset removes.
quality_note: First-party Microsoft support guidance. It applies to the documented client generation and can become stale.

title: Clear the Teams client cache
observation: Microsoft documents different Mac paths for classic and new Teams and says app reset can delete personalization settings.
product_implication: Version-detect Teams before action. Use the owner recipe only after closing the app and stating the settings loss.
quality_note: First-party Microsoft documentation. Paths and client generations are version-specific.

title: Microsoft Teams messages about retention policies
observation: Teams retention can delete messages for every participant and files can have a different policy, leaving a message with a broken file link.
product_implication: Show chat retention and file retention separately. A local file preview is not proof that the source file still exists.
quality_note: First-party Microsoft documentation. Tenant policies vary.

title: File storage in Microsoft Teams
observation: Teams channel files live in SharePoint, while files sent in one-to-one or group chat live in the sender's OneDrive for Business.
product_implication: Report the owner system for each file. A Teams cache action cannot recover a file deleted from OneDrive or SharePoint.
quality_note: First-party Microsoft documentation. It defines current owner storage locations.

title: Create retention policies for Teams and Microsoft 365
observation: Microsoft documents that Teams messages and their referenced OneDrive or SharePoint files can expire under separate policies, leaving File not found links.
product_implication: A cleanup review should show message and file recovery sources as separate objects with separate expiry.
quality_note: First-party Microsoft administrator documentation. Tenant configuration determines actual behavior.

title: Teams chat history appeared gone
observation: A user reported recent history missing from some group chats; the accepted troubleshooting path first compared the web client before clearing local cache.
product_implication: Compare web and desktop state before any reset. If server history is also absent, local data may be recovery material.
quality_note: Direct first-person report on Microsoft Q&A. The accepted answer is guidance, while the symptom is behavior evidence.

title: Users asked how to clear the new Teams cache on Mac
observation: Mac users reported that old Teams cache paths no longer applied after the client changed and asked for a built-in control.
product_implication: Do not reuse stale path rules. Detect bundle and client generation, then cite the current owner action.
quality_note: Direct owner-hosted support discussion. It shows version drift and friction, not a data-loss event.

title: Teams message history disappeared
observation: A user reported Teams message history disappearing and sought both recovery and recurrence prevention.
product_implication: Diagnose server retention, membership, and local cache separately before cleanup. Recovery proof must match the actual cause.
quality_note: Direct first-person report on Microsoft Q&A. It proves the reported symptom, not whether cache or policy caused it.

title: About message history on linked devices
observation: WhatsApp says a linked device stores a local encrypted copy of recent history, but not all phone history is synchronized and deletions sync across online linked devices.
product_implication: Treat Mac history as a partial local store, not a complete cache or backup. Check the phone and link state before reset.
quality_note: First-party WhatsApp documentation. It defines linked-device scope and a known completeness gap.

title: Restore chat history on linked devices
observation: WhatsApp says Web, Mac, and Windows linked devices cannot back up or restore chat history; the phone is required.
product_implication: Do not delete a surviving Mac history under the assumption that it can restore another device, and do not call it a backup.
quality_note: First-party WhatsApp documentation. It establishes an explicit restore limitation.

title: How to restore your chat history
observation: WhatsApp says server systems cannot restore chats, messages after the latest backup are lost, and low device storage can produce a partial backup.
product_implication: Before cleanup, record backup time, size, account, phone number, and free-space proof. Recent local messages may be unrecoverable.
quality_note: First-party WhatsApp documentation. Backup support and requirements can change.

title: How to free up storage on WhatsApp
